BiblicalUsage: Anab was a town in the mountains of Judah, and it is named twice: Joshua cut off the Anakim from Hebron, from Debir, from Anab, and from all the mountains of Judah, and the town is listed again among the cities of Judah's inheritance. It was Anakim country, and Joshua destroyed them utterly with their cities.
TheologicalSignificance: A town named twice still tells the story: Anab was where the giants lived, and Joshua took it. I believe the conquest lists are there so we see God keeping His word town by town, not just in the big battles.
